name: Gardens & growing
description: Patience, soil, and the slow rewards of tending living things.
sentences: A garden teaches patience whether or not you came looking for the lesson.
You plant a seed, cover it with soil, and then nothing seems to happen.
There is no button to press and no way to hurry the roots along.
All you can do is water the ground and trust what is stirring below.
When the first green shoot breaks through, it feels like a small miracle.
Gardeners learn to read the weather and, more often, to forgive it.
Some years the rain comes late, and some years it never seems to stop.
Failure is part of the work, and the answer is simply to plant again.
Growth cannot be forced, only invited by good soil and steady care.
You make the conditions as good as you can and then you let time do the rest.
In a world that prizes speed, a garden insists on its own slow clock.
The tomato ripens when it is ready and not a single day before.
The first bite in late summer is sweeter for the months of quiet tending.
Weeding is dull until you notice how much it resembles clear thinking.
A garden shared is a garden doubled, and good gardeners are generous people.
The surest way to keep a plant alive is often to give a piece of it away.
Bees do more honest work before breakfast than most of us manage all morning.
Even a single pot on a windowsill can change the whole feel of a room.
To tend a living thing is to place a small and hopeful bet on the future.
There is deep comfort in work whose reward you cannot rush or fake.
